tradition.name: Deep ambient
tradition.lineage: A listening and texture label for slowly unfolding, immersive ambient fields. Steve Roach explicitly describes Nostalgia for the Future as deep ambient, while Low Volume Music with Dirk Serries foregrounds overlapping loops. This proposal models the latter layered electronic continuum; the boundary with space ambient is porous and requires Every Noise membership verification.

extras.description: An immersive, low-attack ambient field built from slow electronic layers and overlapping loops. The default combines a gently modulated sustained synthesizer with layered sampled texture. This is an authored realization of a documented deep-ambient listening practice, without a mandatory instrument brand or a claimed geographic origin.
exemplars: Steve Roach — Nostalgia for the Future (2017)
Steve Roach & Dirk Serries — Low Volume Music (2012)

entries.neighbor_distinction: The current space_ambient row already models Roach’s steady-state Immersion branch. This proposal selects overlapping loops and mild timbral modulation, but these are representative defaults rather than an established exclusive genre boundary. Mapping deep ambient to space_ambient cannot be ruled equivalent until the exact source membership is inspected.

tradition.name: Drone
tradition.lineage: Sustained-tone music treats duration, closely controlled pitch and the interaction of held tones as form. Tony Conrad’s amplified violin work supplies the selected bowed-string practice model. Drone also includes electronic and other instrumental practices; this default is neither dark ambient nor a comprehensive instrument roster for all drone music.

extras.description: Long held pitches and subtle interactions among layered tones foreground sustained sound rather than harmonic progression or a beat. This bowed-string default represents Conrad’s amplified, overdubbed violin practice and uses just intonation. Other drone practices use different tunings and sources; neither darkness nor metallic distortion is a defining requirement. Continuous bowing is modeled without a sourced claim of bridge position or classical melodic ornament.

sources.title: Tony Conrad — Four Violins (1964) — Table of the Elements
supported_claims: Conrad’s amplified strings introduced sustained just-intonation drone into minimal music in 1962.
The Dream Syndicate employed long duration and precise pitch; Conrad recorded Four Violins on 19 December 1964.

sources.title: Four Violins — Centre Pompidou
supported_claims: Four sessions of amplified violin were overdubbed.
The artist’s recording studio was 56 Ludlow Street, New York, on 19 December 1964.

entries.neighbor_distinction: Current drone_dark_ambient combines sustained-tone minimalism and dark atmospheric music. This new row isolates sustained pitch/duration without an obligatory dark/horror atmosphere. Current drone_metal, drone_folk and didgeridoo_drone_practice are specific instrumental or scene branches. No existing bare drone/drone_music id exists in the restored catalog, so no rename or equivalent mapping is proposed.
entries.geo_rationale: The museum record locates the documented Four Violins recording at the artist’s studio on Ludlow Street, New York. The pin is a rounded city-center practice anchor, not an exclusive origin or the artist’s birthplace.

tradition.name: Drone psych
tradition.lineage: Psychedelic rock extends guitar sustain and noisy texture into long ensemble improvisation. Bardo Pond’s Philadelphia recordings support a twin-guitar, bass, drums, voice and flute practice; electronics are also documented. The catalog represents the guitar role with one guitar chair, not a claim that the documented band has only one guitarist.

extras.description: A psychedelic ensemble practice in which sustained amplified guitar and dense noise coexist with open-ended collective playing. The chosen Bardo Pond model adds flute and voice to bass and drums, letting instrumental texture lead the vocal song. Specific pickup, drumhead, flute construction and effects settings are author choices, not documented band equipment.

tradition.name: Drone rock
tradition.lineage: A rock practice that builds extended passages from repetitive accompaniment and sustained guitar feedback. Spacemen 3’s live Geneva album is explicitly described as drone rock by its label; Sonic Boom’s firsthand notes describe sustained keys and feedback guitars. The modern recording chain and instrument build choices are representative, not a reconstruction of the 1989 stage rig.

extras.description: Repeated bass/drum accompaniment and long amplified guitar tones support extended rock passages. The selected Spacemen 3 model foregrounds feedback and repetition while retaining a vocal chair. The default describes one reusable studio arrangement, not every track or the exact historical live equipment.
exemplars: Spacemen 3 — Live at the New Morning, Geneva, Switzerland, 18.05.1989

tradition.name: Experimental ambient
tradition.lineage: Ambient composition treats recorded sound, acoustic resonance, noise and electronic montage as mutable material. Tim Hecker’s Ravedeath, 1972 was built from improvised pipe-organ recordings in Reykjavik and extended studio transformation in Montreal. The default models the transformed-recording stage with sampling and granular synthesis, not an assertion that Hecker used a particular sampler or granular algorithm.

extras.description: Recorded acoustic tone, noise and electronic processing form a shifting ambient composition rather than a regular beat or a prescribed mellow pad. The sample/granular roster models Hecker’s studio montage of improvised organ recordings. The acoustic pipe organ is the documented source; these catalog chairs represent its transformed recorded material and do not replace that fact with a hardware claim.

entries.neighbor_distinction: Compared with current ambient/space_ambient sustained-pad defaults, this selected practice makes transformed acoustic source recordings and noise/dissonance central. Compared with dark ambient it does not require horror atmosphere. Sampler plus granular processing is a reusable model of the documented montage practice rather than a universal experimental-ambient roster.
entries.geo_rationale: Hecker’s firsthand interview describes extensive Montreal studio transformation after recording a Reykjavik church organ. Montréal anchors the composition/montage stage represented by this recipe; Reykjavik remains a documented source-recording location.

entries.acoustic_source_model_note: The pipe_organ catalog currently defaults to historical voicing/school/context not established in the Hecker interview. This proposal represents recorded organ material in sample/granular chairs to avoid presenting arbitrary organ-maker defaults as evidence. If integration requires a live source-organ chair, add explicit non-default, auto:false, empty-descriptor unspecified variants for the organ-specific dimensions and verify zero existing recipe drift first.

prerequisites.rationale: Sustained precisely controlled amplified violin is documented, while existing legato-classical and sul-ponticello variants introduce classical melody or undocumented bridge placement. This explicitly selected non-default technique models duration and sustained pitch without changing older recipes.
